statements.t: We believe the Company's improved financial flexibility will allow us to manage periods of market volatility and potential operational disruption while the benefits of the Curragh reset program are delivered.
This program is expected to position the Company to capitalise on favourable metallurgical coal market conditions over the medium to long term.

The Company will continue to prioritise safety as its most important responsibility and remains committed to delivering long-term improvements that create a safer workplace for all employees and contractors.

Through regular site engagements, leadership interactions and workforce participation, the program aims to build a stronger safety culture founded on proactive risk management and shared ownership of safety outcomes.
Together, these measures are intended to drive sustainable improvements in safety performance and support the Company's goal of eliminating serious injuries and fatalities.
Our focus will remain on further optimising this high quality, long-life asset.

While variability can be expected as initiatives continue to be embedded, management believes these results provide early evidence that the program is addressing key operational constraints and improving the production platform.

The Company continues to be supported by AlixPartners and Odin Partnership as implementation progresses and expects initiatives to begin delivering benefits through the remainder of FY2026, with more meaningful benefits expected to be reflected in FY2027.
Having completed the Company's major expansion projects, the focus has shifted from volume-led growth to margin expansion, productivity improvement and cash generation.

The actions we take and decisions we make as we move through the rest of the year are expected to flow through to the full year production outcomes relative to the assumptions underpinning the original guidance, and additional updates will be provided when appropriate.
We will also be considering the most appropriate volumetric guidance metric for the future, in view of our new focus areas.
However, taking into account early savings expected from the reset program, we still expect to achieve our mining cash costs per tonne guidance.

Capital expenditure is currently expected to be toward the lower end of the Company's FY2026 guidance range of US$150 million to US$175 million, reflecting the completion of major growth projects and the Company's continued focus on capital discipline and cash generation.

Reconciliations of certain forward-looking non-GAAP financial measures, including our 2026 mining cost per tonne sold guidance, to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures are not provided because the Company is unable to provide such reconciliations without unreasonable effort, due to the uncertainty and inherent difficulty of predicting the occurrence and the financial impact of items impacting…
